newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs bounce back, end up in lower turnover.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs bounce back, end up in lower turnover.

text.p: Brazilian shares ended 0.98 percent higher Monday after seesawing most of the session, helped by a rise on Wall Street stock prices at the close.
The Bovespa index of the 47 most active stocks closed up 110 points at 11,292 points, after plummeting 15 percent last week.

Total market turnover was a moderate 690.04 million reais ($638.9 million), lower than the market's recent daily average of over one billion reais. Local shares had made losses of over one percent late afternoon, but bounced back at market's close taking their cue from the U.S. stock market.
Analysts said the market is still tense, but they hope that, from now on, it will slowly accumulate at the current market levels amid certain volatility.

They also said they expect selling pressure from local equity funds to ease this week, especially because asset managers already sold heavily last week to cover anticipated withdrawals from retail investors.
"Apparently there were not further heavy sales by funds today," said Germano Guimaraes, director at Primus Asset Management.
Guimaraes also said the market expects fewer fund redemptions in the next few days.
Local equity funds led last week's selling spree, which was triggered by concerns over devaluation.
Traders also cited comments by word-slinger Communications Minister Sergio Motta as a factor that contributed to Monday's stock volatility.
In a interview published in weekly magazine Veja Sunday, Motta strongly criticized ministers and government-allied parties.

Last week, amid the currency turmoil, Motta helped accelerate the market slump by criticizing Central Bank Foreign Affairs director Gustavo Franco. 142 reais. Federal power holding Eletrobras preferred ended up 1.5 percent at 541 reais.
State oil firm Petrobras preferred ended flat at 283 reais.
